sentences.en: extraordinary, is because of a common misconception about the number of people we think we actually
sentences.zh: 之所以非同寻常，是因为我们对实际认识的人数存在一个普遍的误解，

sentences.en: know.
sentences.zh: 即我们认为自己认识的人数。

sentences.en: People think that their address book is essentially the people they know, and it turns out that
sentences.zh: 人们认为他们的通讯录基本上就是他们认识的人，但事实证明，

sentences.en: any particular address book is about 1% of the people they actually know in some way.
sentences.zh: 任何特定的通讯录大约只占他们以某种方式真正认识的人的 1%。

sentences.en: In other words, a neighbor, somebody they bump into in the street, but the address book is
sentences.zh: 换句话说，邻居、街上偶遇的人，但通讯录里的人，

sentences.en: about 1% of the people they know.
sentences.zh: 大约只占他们认识的人的 1%。

sentences.en: As a result, the odds of bumping into someone you know are much greater than you think, because
sentences.zh: 因此，偶遇熟人的几率比你想象的要大得多，因为

sentences.en: you know many more people than you think.
sentences.zh: 你认识的人远比你想象的要多。

sentences.en: Sometimes, math can help us understand the magic.
sentences.zh: 有时，数学可以帮助我们理解这种魔力。

sentences.en: Magic like winning the lottery, not just once, but several times.
sentences.zh: 比如中彩票的魔力，不是一次，而是好几次。

sentences.en: That's what happened to a woman named Joan Ginther.
sentences.zh: 这就是琼·金瑟（Joan Ginther）身上发生的事情。

sentences.en: In 1993, I think it was, she won $5.4 million in Texas Lotto.
sentences.zh: 我想是在 1993 年，她赢得了 540 万美元的德克萨斯州彩票。

sentences.en: Thirteen years later, she won again $2 million.
sentences.zh: 十三年后，她又赢了 200 万美元。

sentences.en: And then a few years after that, she won $3 million.
sentences.zh: 几年后，她又赢了 300 万美元。

sentences.en: And then in 2010, she won $10 million.
sentences.zh: 然后在 2010 年，她赢了 1000 万美元。

sentences.en: What are the odds of one person winning the lottery four times?
sentences.zh: 一个人四次中彩票的几率是多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, the odds are, I think somebody made a calculation, and I did too, that the odds are
sentences.zh: 是的，几率是——我想有人计算过，我也算过——几率大约是

sentences.en: about 18 septillion to one against it happening.
sentences.zh: 18 垓分之一（18 septillion to one）。

sentences.en: Eighteen septillion to one.
sentences.zh: 18 垓分之一。

sentences.en: That's incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: For those who are not mathematicians, a septillion is one followed by 24 zeros.
sentences.zh: 对于非数学家来说，一垓（septillion）就是 1 后面跟着 24 个零。

sentences.en: But Joseph Mazur says, we're actually asking the wrong question.
sentences.zh: 但约瑟夫·马祖尔（Joseph Mazur）说，我们其实问错了问题。

sentences.en: Think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 换个角度想想。

sentences.en: If I buy a lottery ticket, and I ask the question, what are the odds that I will win?
sentences.zh: 如果我买了一张彩票，问自己中奖的几率是多少？

sentences.en: My odds are very small.
sentences.zh: 我的几率非常小。

sentences.en: But if I ask, what are the odds that anyone will win the lottery?
sentences.zh: 但如果我问，任何人中彩票的几率是多少？

sentences.en: In a country of hundreds of millions of people, the odds are actually much higher.
sentences.zh: 在一个拥有数亿人口的国家，这个几率其实要高得多。

sentences.en: So if you ask the question slightly differently, not what are the odds that Joan Ginther will win
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你换个问法，不是问琼·金瑟四次中彩票的几率是多少，

sentences.en: the lottery four times, but what are the odds that anyone will win four times?
sentences.zh: 而是问任何人四次中奖的几率是多少？

sentences.en: You get a very different answer.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一个非常不同的答案。

sentences.en: I think I calculated at one point about five million to one, which is not anywhere near
sentences.zh: 我想我曾计算过，大约是五百万分之一，这与

sentences.en: the septillions.
sentences.zh: 垓分之一相去甚远。

sentences.en: It's about five million to one.
sentences.zh: 大约是五百万分之一。

sentences.en: And that, it takes into account the fact that we have thousands of lotteries in the world.
sentences.zh: 这考虑到了世界上有成千上万种彩票的事实。

sentences.en: I mean, there are many lotteries, and many of them are big-time lotteries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，彩票种类繁多，其中许多还是大型彩票。

sentences.en: So, five million to one, still unlikely, but not incomprehensible.
sentences.zh: 所以，五百万分之一，虽然仍然不太可能，但并非不可理解。

sentences.en: What makes it even more comprehensible is the fact that most lottery winners don't stop
sentences.zh: 让它变得更容易理解的事实是，大多数彩票中奖者在获奖后并不会停止

sentences.en: gambling when they win.
sentences.zh: 赌博。

sentences.en: And you do find that almost everybody who does win a lottery fairly big time spends all that
sentences.zh: 你会发现，几乎所有真正中了大奖的人都会把那笔钱，

sentences.en: money, or much of that money, in trying to win again.
sentences.zh: 或者大部分钱，花在试图再次中奖上。

sentences.en: Joseph Mazur says this might have been the case with Joan Ginther.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·马祖尔说，琼·金瑟的情况可能就是这样。

sentences.en: You win $5.4 million, you have a money to play with.
sentences.zh: 你赢了 540 万美元，就有钱可以玩了。

sentences.en: You have house money.
sentences.zh: 你有的是“庄家的钱”。

sentences.en: So you're taking the house money to bet again, and her odds of winning a second time are better
sentences.zh: 所以你拿着庄家的钱再次下注，她第二次中奖的几率比大多数人都要好，

sentences.en: than most people's because she's got the money to play with.
sentences.zh: 因为她有钱可以玩。

sentences.en: She wins a second time, then she's playing with more money.
sentences.zh: 她第二次中奖后，手里就有更多的钱可以玩了。

sentences.en: And you can see between the first winning and the second winning, it was 13 years.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，第一次中奖和第二次中奖之间隔了 13 年。

sentences.en: Between the second winning and the third, it was only two years.
sentences.zh: 第二次和第三次之间，只隔了两年。

sentences.en: And between the third and the fourth, it was only two years as well.
sentences.zh: 第三次和第四次之间，也只隔了两年。

sentences.en: So Joseph Mazur can wrap his head around what happened to Joan Ginther.
sentences.zh: 所以约瑟夫·马祖尔能够理解琼·金瑟身上发生的事情。

sentences.en: But there are some coincidences that just defy mathematical interpretation.
sentences.zh: 但有些巧合确实无法用数学来解释。

sentences.en: Joseph told me one of his favorite stories about a 19th-century French poet, Emile de Champ.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫给我讲了他最喜欢的故事之一，关于 19 世纪法国诗人埃米尔·德·尚普（Emile de Champ）。

sentences.en: Emile de Champ, as a teenager, he meets a man by the name of a strange name, Monsieur de Fortybou.
sentences.zh: 埃米尔·德·尚普在青少年时期，遇到了一位名字很奇怪的男士，德·福蒂布先生（Monsieur de Fortybou）。

sentences.en: He turns out to be an immigrant from England.
sentences.zh: 原来他是一位来自英国的移民。

sentences.en: And Fortybou introduces him to a plum pudding.
sentences.zh: 福蒂布向他介绍了李子布丁。

sentences.en: It's a very English dish that's almost unheard of in France.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常地道的英式甜点，在法国几乎闻所未闻。

sentences.en: Ten years go by, and de Champ is passing a restaurant in Paris.
sentences.zh: 十年过去了，德·尚普路过巴黎的一家餐馆。

sentences.en: There's a sign on the window saying that they have plum pudding on their menu.
sentences.zh: 窗户上的招牌写着他们的菜单上有李子布丁。

sentences.en: But when de Champ goes inside, he's told the last of the plum pudding was just sold to a gentleman sitting in the back.
sentences.zh: 但当德·尚普进去时，被告知最后一份李子布丁刚刚卖给了一位坐在后面的绅士。

sentences.en: The waiter calls out loud,
sentences.zh: 服务员大声喊道：

sentences.en: Monsieur de Fortybou, would you be willing to share your plum pudding with this gentleman?
sentences.zh: “德·福蒂布先生，您愿意和这位先生分享您的李子布丁吗？”

sentences.en: Years pass.
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝。

sentences.en: De Champ is now at a dinner party with some friends.
sentences.zh: 德·尚普现在正和朋友们参加晚宴。

sentences.en: The host announces an unusual dessert will be served.
sentences.zh: 主人宣布将上一道不寻常的甜点。

sentences.en: Plum pudding.
sentences.zh: 李子布丁。

sentences.en: And de Champ jokes that one of the guests to arrive must be Monsieur de Fortybou.
sentences.zh: 德·尚普开玩笑说，即将到来的客人中一定有德·福蒂布先生。

sentences.en: Well, soon the doorbell rings, and Monsieur de Fortybou is announced, and he enters.
sentences.zh: 果然，门铃响了，德·福蒂布先生被通报进来，他走了进来。

sentences.en: He's an old man by now.
sentences.zh: 他现在已经是一位老人了。

sentences.en: But de Champ recognizes him.
sentences.zh: 但德·尚普认出了他。

sentences.en: Monsieur de Fortybou looks around and realizes that he's in the wrong apartment.
sentences.zh: 德·福蒂布先生环顾四周，意识到自己走错了公寓。

sentences.en: He was invited to a dinner, but not in that apartment.
sentences.zh: 他受邀参加晚宴，但不是在那间公寓。

sentences.en: I love that because it's, you know, it's a triple coincidence, and it has a beautiful story element with it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事，因为它是一个三重巧合，而且带有一个美丽的故事元素。

sentences.en: I mean, that's so magnificent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太壮观了。

sentences.en: And that's why, that's the kind of coincidence I love to hear.
sentences.zh: 这就是我喜欢听的那种巧合。

sentences.en: Joseph Mazur, professor of mathematics and author of Fluke, The Math and Myth of Coincidence.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·马祖尔，数学教授，《巧合：数学与神话》（Fluke, The Math and Myth of Coincidence）一书的作者。

sentences.en: When we come back, we're going to look at what coincidences reveal about the mind.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨巧合揭示了关于思维的什么信息。

sentences.en: In particular, I'm fascinated by something I've observed in my own life.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我对自己在生活中观察到的一些现象很着迷。

sentences.en: When I experience a coincidence, it invariably feels more meaningful to me than it does to others.
sentences.zh: 当我经历巧合时，它对我来说总是比对其他人更有意义。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: I'm fascinated by coincidences and could listen for hours to stories about them.
sentences.zh: 我对巧合很着迷，可以花几个小时听关于它们的故事。

sentences.en: But what is it that so fascinates us about these moments in life?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让我们对生活中的这些时刻如此着迷呢？

sentences.en: At the University of Chicago, psychologist Nick Epley thinks he might have one answer.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥大学，心理学家尼克·埃普利（Nick Epley）认为他可能有一个答案。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book, Mind Wise.
sentences.zh: 他是《思维智慧》（Mind Wise）一书的作者。

sentences.en: To understand how Epley thinks about coincidences,
sentences.zh: 为了理解埃普利是如何看待巧合的，

sentences.en: I need to take a moment and explain his broader work to you firSt.
sentences.zh: 我需要先花点时间向你解释他更广泛的研究工作。

sentences.en: Epley's book examines how we read the mental states and intentions of other people.
sentences.zh: 埃普利的书研究了我们如何解读他人的心理状态和意图。

sentences.en: This is a remarkably useful skill, but we sometimes misapply it.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常实用的技能，但我们有时会误用它。

sentences.en: We sometimes attribute intentionality to things that aren't even living,
sentences.zh: 我们有时会将意图归因于甚至没有生命的东西，

sentences.en: especially when they're out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当它们不同寻常的时候。

sentences.en: For example, we don't personify a sunny day, but we give hurricanes a name.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们不会将晴天人格化，但我们会给飓风起名字。

sentences.en: Katrina, Sandy, Andrew.
sentences.zh: 卡特里娜、桑迪、安德鲁。

sentences.en: After Hurricane Katrina, the mayor of New Orleans said,
sentences.zh: 卡特里娜飓风过后，新奥尔良市长说：

sentences.en: God must be mad at America.
sentences.zh: “上帝一定是在对美国发火。”

sentences.en: This isn't new.
sentences.zh: 这并不新鲜。

sentences.en: For centuries, people have ascribed intentionality to natural forces.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人们一直将意图归因于自然力量。

sentences.en: We think storms, droughts, and earthquakes must have a mind of their own.
sentences.zh: 我们认为风暴、干旱和地震一定有它们自己的思想。

sentences.en: This general tendency to explain behaviors in terms of purpose or intent or meaning
sentences.zh: 这种用目的、意图或意义来解释行为的普遍倾向，

sentences.en: is often quite a successful thing to do.
sentences.zh: 通常是非常成功的。

sentences.en: It turns out we live with other people who do have intentions and goals and foresight
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我们生活在其他人中间，他们确实有意图、目标、远见、

sentences.en: and planning and meaning behind their actions.
sentences.zh: 计划，并且他们的行为背后有意义。

sentences.en: And so, by and large, that tendency to make those kinds of attributions to other people
sentences.zh: 所以，总的来说，那种对他人进行此类归因的倾向，

sentences.en: is a good way to learn about each other,
sentences.zh: 是了解彼此的好方法，

sentences.en: is a good way to explain why other people did something in the past,
sentences.zh: 是解释为什么别人在过去做了某事的好方法，

sentences.en: to predict how they're likely to behave in the future.
sentences.zh: 也是预测他们未来可能如何表现的好方法。

sentences.en: But the problem with any kind of good tool is that sometimes we use it a little too much.
sentences.zh: 但任何好工具的问题在于，有时我们用得有点过头了。

sentences.en: And that's what happens in these cases,
sentences.zh: 这就是在这些情况下发生的事情，

sentences.en: where you're trying to explain the behavior of something
sentences.zh: 当你试图解释某件事的行为时，

sentences.en: that doesn't really have a sensible explanation for it.
sentences.zh: 而这件事其实并没有合理的解释。

sentences.en: Some random event, some chance occurrence, some physical anomaly,
sentences.zh: 一些随机事件、一些偶然发生的事情、一些物理异常、

sentences.en: some weather pattern that crops up that might not, in fact, have a mind behind it.
sentences.zh: 一些突然出现的、实际上可能背后并没有思想的天气模式。

sentences.en: This is why we're fascinated by robots that move in unpredictable ways.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们对以不可预测方式移动的机器人如此着迷。

sentences.en: What we found was that when people were given a description of an object
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们得到一个物体的描述，

sentences.en: that made it sound unpredictable, like you couldn't anticipate its actions,
sentences.zh: 让它听起来不可预测，就像你无法预料它的行动一样，

sentences.en: that's when people described it or reported that it had more mental states.
sentences.zh: 那时人们就会描述它，或者报告说它具有更多的心理状态。

sentences.en: They were more willing to say that the object has a mind of its own,
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意说这个物体有自己的思想，

sentences.en: that it has intentions, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，它有自己的意图。

sentences.en: And I don't think this is totally counterintuitive, that it is a mind,
sentences.zh: 我不认为这完全违背直觉，即它是一个思想，

sentences.en: if you see, for instance, a billiard ball sitting on a table,
sentences.zh: 如果你看到，例如，一个台球放在桌子上，

sentences.en: another ball comes along and hits it,
sentences.zh: 另一个球过来撞击它，

sentences.en: and that ball rolls off in the predicted direction,
sentences.zh: 然后那个球按预期的方向滚走，

sentences.en: well, you don't need anything to explain that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你不需要任何东西来解释这一点。

sentences.en: But if you've got a ball sitting on a table,
sentences.zh: 但如果你有一个球放在桌子上，

sentences.en: and it suddenly starts rolling around randomly,
sentences.zh: 它突然开始随机滚动，

sentences.en: well, then you've got something to explain.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那你就有东西需要解释了。

sentences.en: And in these cases, sometimes people look to the inside of an agent,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，有时人们会看向代理的内部，

sentences.en: give it a mind, maybe the ball is possessed,
sentences.zh: 赋予它一个思想，也许球被附身了，

sentences.en: maybe there's a demon controlling it, moving it around the table.
sentences.zh: 也许有一个恶魔在控制它，在桌子上移动它。

sentences.en: Sometimes people attribute a mind to something when it's not there,
sentences.zh: 有时人们在某物不存在思想时也会赋予它思想，

sentences.en: but they do that as an effort to explain what's going on in this autonomous agent.
sentences.zh: 但他们这样做是为了努力解释这个自主代理正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And they're more likely to do that when an agent behaves somewhat unpredictably.
sentences.zh: 当一个代理的行为有些不可预测时，他们更有可能这样做。

sentences.en: I was over at a friend's house, and my friend has a wonderful pool,
sentences.zh: 我当时在朋友家，我的朋友有一个很棒的游泳池，

sentences.en: and he had set this underwater Roomba, for the lack of a better term,
sentences.zh: 他设置了这个水下 Roomba（姑且这么称呼吧），

sentences.en: to clean the bottom of the pool.
sentences.zh: 来清洁游泳池的底部。

sentences.en: So it sort of rolls around the bottom of the pool,
sentences.zh: 所以它在游泳池底部滚动，

sentences.en: and it goes in this completely random fashion, right?
sentences.zh: 它以这种完全随机的方式运行，对吧？

sentences.en: So it just runs for a couple of hours.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是运行了几个小时。

sentences.en: It's cleaning the bottom of the pool.
sentences.zh: 它在清洁游泳池的底部。

sentences.en: And I found myself fascinated just watching it,
sentences.zh: 我发现自己光是看着它就很着迷，

sentences.en: because the fact that you can't predict what it's going to do next
sentences.zh: 因为你无法预测它下一步要做什么的事实，

sentences.en: makes it just more interesting and more alive, in a way,
sentences.zh: 使它在某种程度上比以非常可预测的方式移动的东西，

sentences.en: than something that moves in a very predictable fashion.
sentences.zh: 更有趣、更生动。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Something that moves robotically, very predictably,
sentences.zh: 以机器人般、非常可预测的方式移动的东西，

sentences.en: that is just a mindless machine.
sentences.zh: 那只是一台无脑的机器。

sentences.en: But when your Roomba is going around randomly,
sentences.zh: 但当你的 Roomba 随机四处走动时，

sentences.en: well, now it wants to go over there a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在它想往那边去一点。

sentences.en: Now it wants to move over here.
sentences.zh: 现在它想往这边移动。

sentences.en: Now it realizes it didn't clean that side of the pool over there.
sentences.zh: 现在它意识到它没有清理游泳池那边的那一侧。

sentences.en: Things that behave randomly start to get a little sense of a mind.
sentences.zh: 表现出随机行为的事物，开始让人产生一种它们有思想的错觉。

sentences.en: Now, people aren't crazy.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们并没有疯。

sentences.en: You don't think it's like your mother, right?
sentences.zh: 你不会觉得它像你母亲，对吧？

sentences.en: Or your spouse who's vacuuming the living room.
sentences.zh: 或者像正在客厅吸尘的配偶。

sentences.en: But it starts to look just a little bit more mindful.
